extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants and attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating prior art and statutory exceptions under the AIA (35 U.S.C. 102) in patent examination, including grace-period inventor disclosures, inventor-originated disclosures, and treatment of U.S. patent documents and WIPO publications for prior art purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace Period Inventor Or Inventor-Originated Disclosure Exception (AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure which would otherwise qualify as prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) is not prior art if the disclosure was (1) one year or less before the effective filing date of the claimed invention; and (2) by the inventor or a joint inventor, or by another who obtained the subject matter directly or indirectly from the inventor or joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exceptions limit use of an inventor's own work as prior art when publicly disclosed by inventor/joint inventor or one who obtained the subject matter from them within one year of the effective filing date. See MPEP §2153.01(a) and §2153.01(b) for discussion of inventor disclosures and inventor-originated disclosures respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a disclosure is 'apparent' from the disclosure or the application/specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Office personnel will not apply a disclosure as prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) if it is apparent from the disclosure itself that it is by the inventor or a joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests for being 'apparent' from the disclosure: (1) the disclosure was made one year or less before the effective filing date; (2) the disclosure names the inventor or a joint inventor as an author or an inventor; and (3) the disclosure does not name additional persons as authors on a printed publication or joint inventors on a patent. Examples: if the application names A,B,C as inventors and the publication names A,B as authors (within one year), the publication is apparent as an inventor disclosure and not prior art. If the publication names more authors than the application lists as inventors, it may not be apparent and may be treated as prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant designation of grace period inventor disclosures in the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can include a statement designating any grace period inventor disclosures in the specification (see 37 CFR 1.77(b)(6) and MPEP §608.01(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of the specified format is not required, nor is identification of prior disclosures by the inventor/joint inventor required unless necessary to overcome a rejection, but identifying prior disclosures may expedite examination and save costs. If the specification specifically references a grace period inventor disclosure (and it does not name additional authors/joint inventors), the Office will consider it apparent that the disclosure is by the inventor/joint inventor. Applicants may also provide a copy of the prior disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of affidavits or declarations (37 CFR 1.130) to establish exceptions under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office provides a mechanism for filing an affidavit or declaration (under 37 CFR 1.130) to establish that a disclosure is not prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) due to an exception in AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where it is not apparent from the prior disclosure or the application/specification that the disclosure is by the inventor or joint inventor (or by another who obtained the subject matter therefrom), the applicant may establish the exception by affidavit/declaration. See MPEP §§717, 718, 2155.01, 2155.02, and 2155.03 for procedures and use of affidavits/declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Exception Under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(B) (Inventor Or Inventor-Originated Prior Public Disclosure Exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure which would otherwise qualify as prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) may be disqualified as prior art if (1) the disclosure was made one year or less before the effective filing date; and (2) the subject matter disclosed had been previously publicly disclosed by the inventor, a joint inventor, or another who obtained the subject matter directly or indirectly from the inventor or joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus is on the 'subject matter' that had been publicly disclosed earlier by the inventor or person who obtained it from the inventor. Mode of disclosure need not match (patent, publication, public use, sale); nor must the earlier disclosure be verbatim. Examples: if inventor previously disclosed elements A,B,C and intervening disclosure shows A,B,C,D, only D is available as prior art. If inventor disclosed a species and intervening disclosure discloses the genus, the intervening genus disclosure is excepted; converse (genus then species) is not excepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) 'U.S. Patent Documents'
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) sets forth types of U.S. patent documents available as prior art as of the date they were effectively filed with respect to the subject matter relied upon if they name another inventor: (1) U.S. patents; (2) U.S. patent application publications; and (3) certain WIPO published applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These 'U.S. patent documents' may be prior art even if their issue/publication date is not before the effective filing date, if they were 'effectively filed' earlier. See MPEP §2152.01 for 'effective filing date' and AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d) for criteria when subject matter was effectively filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of WIPO PCT published applications for AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The WIPO publication of a PCT international application that designates the United States is an application for patent deemed published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) for purposes of AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) under 35 U.S.C. 374.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the AIA, WIPO publications of PCT applications that designate the United States are treated as U.S. patent application publications for prior art purposes regardless of the international filing date, English language, or whether the PCT application enters the U.S. national stage. This differs from pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) treatment, where additional conditions applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining When Subject Matter Was Effectively Filed Under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. patent, U.S. patent application publication, or WIPO published application is prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) with respect to any subject matter described in the document as of either its actual filing date or the filing date of a prior application to which a priority or benefit claim is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A document is 'entitled to claim' priority/benefit if it: (1) contains a priority/benefit claim to the prior application; (2) was filed within the applicable filing period (copending or within 12 months as applicable); and (3) has a common inventor or same applicant. For 102(d) prior art purposes, the Office need not evaluate whether any claim is actually entitled to priority/benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119/120/121/365/386. A prior-filed application relied upon must describe the subject matter but need not meet 35 U.S.C. 112(a) enablement. The AIA eliminates the Hilmer doctrine; foreign priority dates (earliest such application that describes the subject matter) can make a U.S. patent document effectively filed earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of 'Names Another Inventor' for AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify as prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2), the prior U.S. patent document must 'name[] another inventor.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any difference in inventive entity between the prior art U.S. patent document and the application under examination means the prior document satisfies the 'names another inventor' requirement. In joint-inventor situations, only one joint inventor needs to be different. Even if one or more joint inventors are common, the U.S. patent document qualifies as prior art under 102(a)(2) unless an exception under 102(b)(2) applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Exception Under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(A) (Inventor-Originated Disclosure Exception to 102(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(A) provides that a disclosure which would otherwise qualify as prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) may be disqualified as prior art if the subject matter disclosed was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the subject matter in a U.S. patent document relied upon is by another who obtained the subject matter from the inventor or a joint inventor, the applicant may establish the exception by affidavit or declaration. See MPEP §2155.03 for use of affidavits/declarations to show disclosure was by another who obtained the subject matter from the inventor or joint inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Exception Under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(B) (Inventor or Inventor-Originated Prior Public Disclosure Exception to 102(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(B) provides that a U.S. patent document which would otherwise qualify as prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) may be disqualified as prior art if the subject matter disclosed had been previously publicly disclosed by the inventor, a joint inventor, or another who obtained the subject matter directly or indirectly from the inventor or joint inventor, before the date the subject matter relied upon was effectively filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exception focuses on the 'subject matter' previously publicly disclosed; there is no requirement that mode of disclosure be the same or verbatim. If inventor previously disclosed A,B,C and intervening U.S. patent document discloses A,B,C,D, only D is available as prior art. Genus/species examples apply as in 102(b)(1)(B). Determination of applicability does not involve comparing the claimed invention to either disclosure; it concerns whether the intervening document's subject matter was previously publicly disclosed by the inventor (or person who obtained it from the inventor). See MPEP §§2155.02 and 2155.03 for affidavits/declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Exception Under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) (Common Ownership or Obligation of Assignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) provides an exception to AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) based on common ownership or obligation of assignment between the parties/applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This entry is the section header for the common ownership/obligation of assignment exception (MPEP §2154.02(c)). Detailed application guidance is in the cited MPEP section (not included in this chunk).
